title: Reckoner
feel: Floating, legato picked line over busy shuffling percussion

alt_voicings.label: Open-chord reduction & bridge option
alt_voicings.note: open chords for strumming along only; G6 can replace Em/G in the bridge

sections.name: Intro (riff ×2)
sections.bars: C | Em | D . Dsus4 D | C | Em
sections.note: Riff chords shown as version A (top-three-string triads). Bar lengths approximate — follow the record.

sections.name: Verse
sections.bars: Em | D | C | Em | C | Em D | A C
sections.note: Loop the first five bars (decorate D with Dsus4–D); each verse ends with the last two (A = open A in every reduction).

sections.name: Bridge
sections.bars: Emaj7/G# | Em/G | Am | Cmaj7 | B7/D# | Cmaj7 | Am | B
sections.note: Arpeggiated. Chromatic bass G♯ – G – A.

why: High, ringing **top-string triads** up the neck with sus4 grace changes, and a bridge with a chromatic bass and a maj7 voicing. The record has three guitars, so every one-guitar version is a reduction.
hard_change: Version A: **Em (fret 12) → D (frets 11-10)**, a two-finger shift with a stretch. In the bridge: **Emaj7/G♯ (thumb) → Em/G**.
theory: Analysed as E minor (no published key). Verse i–VII–VI Aeolian; the A is IV major (Dorian colour). Bridge: E/G♯ (V of iv) → i6 → iv → VI → V7/D♯ → VI → iv → V.
steps: Changes alone, slowly: Em → D → C triads, then Dsus4–D as a grace change.
With the rhythm at 70% (about 73 bpm): roll each triad as the record does.
With the record; then the bridge arpeggios on their own.
tips: Two common ways to teach the riff: **version A** (the chart: top-three-string triads, closest to the record's tone; the inversions keep plain names in the grid) and **version B** (strings 5-4-2). Where either differs from what your teacher showed you, **use your teacher's voicings**.
caveat: Voicings vary between transcriptions (three guitars) — trust your ear and your teacher's version. Harmony, tuning and no capo are certain.
